title: Pit Chaos Handling with Passes
description: Players inside a faceoff circle stickhandle through traffic while players around the outside move a separate puck. Rotate groups after short work intervals. Emphasize scanning, finding open ice, presenting passing targets and making the next play before the puck arrives.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan constantly.
Find open space while handling the puck.
Outside passers should think one play ahead.
Progress to one-touch or two-touch passing for advanced groups.

title: Puck Race to Possession Game
description: Two players race to a loose puck inside a circle. The winner protects possession under pressure. On a second whistle the puck carrier attacks the net while the defender works to recover and return possession to the coach.
coaching_points: Win the puck line with body position.
Protect the puck with hips and shoulders while keeping the feet moving.
Avoid reaching; stay in a strong skating posture.
Transition immediately from protection to attack.

title: Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1
description: Play a 2-on-1 inside a constrained corner-to-half-wall area. The offense works to complete a set number of passes before attacking the net, while the defender wins by creating turnovers or forcing the puck out of the area.
coaching_points: Use the boards as an extra passing option.
Protect the puck until a passing lane opens.
Move immediately after passing.
Defend with active sticks, stops and starts.

title: Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)
description: Two offensive players and one defender compete inside a small cross-ice area. The offense must connect on a prescribed number of passes before earning a shot; the defender earns an attacking chance by disrupting possession.
coaching_points: Move without the puck.
Protect first, then expose the puck to pass.
Defend with active sticks and stops and starts.
Encourage pass-and-move and give-and-go habits.

title: Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game
description: Players score by passing through small gates placed around a confined area. Change the number and size of gates, available space, player count, obstacles and competitive rules to scale difficulty.
coaching_points: Play with the head up.
Move to open space after every pass.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication.
Reduce space or gate size to increase decision speed.

title: NZ Give and Go
description: Play 2-on-2 in the neutral zone with a support player on the blue line who can activate to create a temporary 3-on-2. The possession team uses movement after the pass to generate give-and-go options and new passing lanes.
coaching_points: Move immediately after passing.
Work off defenders' heels to create new lanes.
Know the next destination before moving the puck.
Look to get the puck back instead of circling the perimeter.

title: Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush
description: The drill begins with a 1-on-1 rush. On the next whistle a second rush starts the opposite way while the original pair joins, turning the sequence into a continuous 2-on-2.
coaching_points: Angle with speed while skating forward.
Defenders communicate through the transition.
Backcheck tightly and stay connected.
Recognize the shift from 1-on-1 to 2-on-2 quickly.

title: 2 v 3 Entry Offense vs. Breakout Transition
description: Start with a 2-on-2 rush plus a backchecker to create a 2-on-3. After the defending team wins possession, it immediately supports the puck and breaks out while two new attackers enter, creating the next repetition.
coaching_points: Transition immediately after possession changes.
Get two players to the puck on the breakout.
Move the puck before the opposition can organize.
Use the format to teach entries, re-entries and rush reads.

title: Buffalo 2v2 to 3v3 to 4v4
description: Begin with a 2-on-2 rush. On successive whistles add one player per team with a new puck, progressing to 3-on-3 and then 4-on-4 before resetting the repetition.
coaching_points: Attack quickly before defenders are set.
Support the puck by moving to open ice.
Backcheck with sticks on the ice and keep attackers outside.
Transition to offense immediately after regaining possession.

title: 3 on 3 Add a D
description: Play 3-on-3 on a shortened rink with one stationary support defenseman behind each team's net. A team activates its extra D by completing a pass behind the net, creating a 4-on-3 until possession changes.
coaching_points: Encourage defensemen to join the rush.
Look for weak-side speed.
Transition quickly when possession changes.
Recognize when activating the extra player creates an advantage.

title: The Ricky
description: Two groups race to complete a clean breakout. The first group to move the puck through its breakout sequence earns the first puck for a 3-on-3 attack at the far end. The second group must still finish its breakout before joining the game.
coaching_points: Use efficient breakout routes and crisp tape-to-tape passes.
Keep sticks available as passing targets.
Communicate and shoulder-check before receiving the puck.
Finish the breakout before transitioning into the 3-on-3.

title: 1, 2, 3, Forecheck
description: A progressive full-ice forecheck and breakout drill. The breakout group first exits against one forechecker, then two, and finally a full three-forward forecheck before the sequence opens into 5-on-5 play.
coaching_points: Forecheckers angle with sticks on the ice and force play outside.
Breakout players communicate and scan before receiving.
Wingers get low enough to become reliable outlets.
Center supports underneath with a low-and-slow route.

title: The Gambler
description: Both sides begin with a point shot and net-front timing. The play then turns into a rush where a support forward chooses which side to join, creating a changing 1-on-1, 2-on-1 or 3-on-1 for the defender to read.
coaching_points: Support forwards scan before choosing which rush to join.
Attackers move the puck quickly when numbers create an advantage.
Defenders identify the rush numbers early and manage gap.
Use active sticks to take away the middle passing lane.

title: 2 v 2 Rim Game
description: A continuous 2-on-2 starts with a rim around the boards and a clean pickup. Offense attacks the net while defense tries to win possession and move the puck to the next players waiting in line, which immediately starts the next repetition.
coaching_points: Rim the puck with purpose and use the boards' angle.
Receive the rim cleanly before making the next play.
Defenders communicate and angle with active sticks.
Transition quickly when possession changes.

title: 6 on 3 Monkey in the Middle
description: Six offensive players surround three defenders in a half-zone possession game. The offense scores by moving the puck through the defending group while the defenders work together to close lanes, pressure the puck and recover possession.
coaching_points: Offense scans before receiving and uses deception to open seams.
Use same-side support when the cross-ice lane is closed.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and maintain inside positioning.
The pressure defender angles the puck carrier toward limited options.

title: RPI 2 on 2
description: A continuous 2-on-2 that begins with attackers approaching the blue line while two defenders work to deny entry. If defense wins the puck, it moves the puck to the next pair, and the previous attackers become the new defenders.
coaching_points: Defenders manage gap and protect the blue line.
Use stick position and body angle to force attackers outside.
Attackers keep feet moving and recognize when a chip is the better entry.
Transition roles immediately after possession changes.

title: 4 v 2 Rondo to 4 v 2 Quick Attack
description: Part 1 is a 4-on-2 rondo around a faceoff circle. On the second whistle the coach places a new puck in the corner and the same players immediately transition into a 4-on-2 quick attack toward the net.
coaching_points: Offense scans, supports and uses deception before the pass.
Keep sticks ready as clear passing targets.
Defense keeps sticks in lanes and communicates.
On the second whistle, transition to the attack immediately.

title: The Box Game
description: A 2-on-2 begins in-zone with a support player at the blue line for each team. After every possession change, the new offensive team must use its support player before attacking, creating constant give-and-go and net-front decisions.
coaching_points: Use the support player quickly after gaining possession.
Move immediately after passing to create a return option.
Defenders protect the middle with sticks in lanes.
Support players make quick pass-or-shot decisions.

title: Slovakian Scoring Game
description: Two teams race through a sequence of scoring situations: 1-on-0, 2-on-0, 2-on-1 and 3-on-2. A team continues only after scoring; a miss turns the next attempt over to the opponent.
coaching_points: Attack each situation with game pace.
Recognize the numerical advantage and use it quickly.
Defenders must be ready to enter immediately for the 2-on-1 and 3-on-2.
Keep the game competitive by tracking progression.

title: Ferrari 3 on 2
description: A high-tempo full-ice 3-on-2 rush drill. A forward curls to receive a pass at the far blue line, a second forward joins with speed, and a third forward activates to complete the 3-on-2 while two defenders gap through the middle.
coaching_points: Forwards communicate, fill lanes and attack with speed.
Get off the wall to create width and passing options.
Defenders match the rush speed and establish gap early.
Use active sticks to protect the middle and force play outside.

title: Circle Puck Protect
description: Two players battle for a loose puck inside a faceoff circle. On the next whistle the player with possession attacks down ice while the other player transitions into an angling defender. The puck carrier must stay outside until crossing the red line before attacking the middle.
coaching_points: Compete low and use body position to protect the puck.
Defender matches speed, keeps the stick down and steers the attacker wide.
Puck carrier scans for a chance to cut inside only after crossing the red line.
Drive wide to the net when the middle is closed.

title: 2 V 2 Crossfire Box Game With Outlets
description: Four players compete inside a marked box while two permanent flank outlets support the team in possession. The offensive pair uses the outlets to create quick-touch scoring chances. A turnover immediately changes the two players inside the box from offense to defense.
coaching_points: Use deception and quick touches to create space.
Players without the puck must work into clear passing lanes with sticks available.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and protect the middle.
Transition immediately after a turnover.

title: 2 V 2 Tire Pass Game With Support
description: Play 2-on-2 in the middle with four gated support players positioned around the outside. Teams score by connecting a pass to a teammate inside a gate, then immediately moving to support the next play. Rotate inside and outside groups in short competitive shifts.
coaching_points: After passing, move immediately to become the next outlet.
Support players stay available and present a clear target.
Defenders angle play outside and use sticks to close passing lanes.
Keep the game competitive by tracking points.

title: 2 V 0 Continuous Backcheck
description: A pair attacks 2-on-0 from a coach's pass and finishes at the net. As the next pair starts the opposite way, the first pair immediately becomes the backchecking pressure. The sequence continues end to end.
coaching_points: Attack with pace and finish at the net.
Backcheckers recover relentlessly with sticks on the ice.
Transition from offense to defense immediately.
Keep spacing so the rush remains game-like.

title: Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up
description: Four lines face one another in the neutral zone while multiple pucks are active at the same time. Puck carriers scan for an open player across the ice, pass, and continue moving. The drill stays continuous and forces awareness, communication and passing under traffic.
coaching_points: Keep eyes up and scan before receiving or passing.
Explode away from the line.
Communicate early.
Keep sticks on the ice as targets.
Add a fifth puck to raise the difficulty.

title: Griffs 2 V 2 Game
description: Play 2-on-2 in the neutral zone with two support defensemen behind each team's net. Using a defenseman triggers an automatic D-to-D pass and activates one defenseman into the rush, creating a 3-on-2 attack before the player returns to the support position.
coaching_points: Communicate and support the puck in the neutral zone.
On the rush, fill middle and wide lanes.
Activated defenseman joins with purpose, then recovers to the support position.
Defenders keep active sticks and angle attackers outside.

title: Offensive Advantage Game
description: Two separate 2-on-1 situations share the zone. Players on the weak side can activate across the divider, turning the play into a 3-on-1 or 3-on-2. The constraint forces quick decisions about when to join the attack and when leaving an opponent unattended is too risky.
coaching_points: Players without the puck decide quickly whether activation creates an advantage.
Communicate before crossing to the other side.
Use quick releases and one-touch plays in tight space.
Always leave at least one offensive player on the original side.

title: Redwing 2 V 3 or 2 V 4
description: Three or four power-play players retrieve a dump and try to break out against two aggressive penalty-kill forecheckers. The drill isolates PP breakout decisions while the PK works on first-pressure speed and taking away the middle outlet.
coaching_points: First PK forechecker attacks the puck with speed.
Second PK forechecker removes the middle lane.
Power-play players support underneath the puck and communicate exits.
Reset with a new group after each breakout attempt.

title: Double Gates Activation Game
description: A 1-on-1 starts in the corner with two gates positioned beside the net. When the attacker carries through a gate, a high support player activates and the play becomes a 2-on-1. The defender tries to win possession and exit the zone.
coaching_points: Puck carrier shoulder-checks and protects until ready to make a play.
Use the net and boards to shield pressure.
Defender closes with a good angle and an active stick.
After gate activation, attack quickly before the defender can reset.

title: 3 vs. 3 Corner Drill
description: Play 3-on-3 around a faceoff circle with a net on each side. Each team may place only one player inside the circle while the other two remain outside. This creates constant inside-out passing, quick shots and communication under pressure.
coaching_points: Move the puck quickly and shoot without overhandling.
Outside players move to become clear outlets.
Communicate and present the stick as a target.
Defenders keep sticks down to block interior passing lanes.

title: Hit The Tire Passing Game WIth No Goalie
description: Play 3-on-3 in one zone with a tire on each faceoff dot as the scoring target. The attacking team works the puck quickly to create a lane to the far tire while staying outside that offensive circle.
coaching_points: Use deception and tight turns to open passing lanes.
Players without the puck jump to open ice with sticks available.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and protect the middle.
Use the no-goalie format when you want a competitive passing game.

title: Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)
description: Play 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 in-zone. Offense scores on the goalie, while the defending team earns points by winning possession and carrying the puck through a gate above the circles. Roles flip on the next shift.
coaching_points: Offense creates 2-on-1s, drives the net and supports loose pucks.
Defense communicates man-to-man responsibilities and turns recoveries into controlled exits.
Players must recognize the immediate offense-to-defense transition.
Keep shifts short and competitive.

title: Perry Pearn Tracking Game
description: Play 3-on-3 below the tops of the circles. The offensive team attacks until the defense wins the puck and carries it across the top-of-circles line. On every turnover, the former attackers must track through the puck and stop the controlled exit.
coaching_points: Track above and through the puck on a 45-degree angle.
All three players react together on possession changes.
Offense extends zone time and forces the defense to work under fatigue.
Scale the game to 2-on-2, 3-on-3 or 4-on-4.

title: Buffalo 12 Player Small Area Game
description: A 3-on-3 plays cross-ice while each team has three stationary bumper players around its offensive side. The bumpers may pass, shoot and defend but stay outside the central playing area, creating frequent numerical advantages.
coaching_points: Scan for bumper options before pressure arrives.
Use cross-ice passes, one-touch plays and quick shots.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and avoid chasing harmless board possession.
Transition immediately through a teammate or bumper after a turnover.

title: 1 v 1 Puck Retrieval to 2 v 1
description: A defender and forechecker race around the dot to a puck placed in the corner. The player who wins the retrieval must find an outlet in a gate, which immediately creates a 2-on-1 attack.
coaching_points: Retriever shoulder-checks and uses deception before touching the puck.
Forechecker angles with the stick down to remove space and lanes.
Outlet explodes out of the gate after receiving the pass.
Rotate players through retrieval, forecheck and outlet roles.

title: 1 v 1 Use The Net
description: A defender starts with the puck behind the net and tries to escape an angling forechecker by using the net as protection before skating through a gate. If the forechecker wins the puck, the forechecker attacks the net.
coaching_points: Both players keep their heads up and read the pressure.
Forechecker creates an angle instead of chasing directly.
Puck carrier uses the net, deception and patience to create separation.
Adjust gate size or location to change difficulty.

title: Anchorage Cut-back Drill
description: A continuous half-ice drill built around a give-and-go behind the net. The puck carrier uses a cutback behind the goal to escape pressure, then finds the supporting player in the slot for a quick finish.
coaching_points: Sell the route before making the cutback.
Use the area behind the net to create separation.
Support player mirrors the puck and arrives in the slot on time.
Keep the exchange and shot quick so the drill stays continuous.

title: Road Runner 3 v 2
description: A continuous 3-on-2 rush drill. After the first rush attacks, the next group starts the opposite way and the original F3 tracks back through the neutral zone, turning the next sequence into a 3-on-3.
coaching_points: Attackers get the puck to middle ice and use weak-side speed.
Defenders establish gap early and protect the middle.
F3 stays above the puck and tracks with urgency.
Sort responsibilities quickly as the rush changes from 3-on-2 to 3-on-3.

title: Breakout Transition Game
description: A 2-on-2 attacks while the defending pair tries to win the puck and connect a breakout pass to teammates waiting at the center divider. Once that pass is completed, the waiting pair attacks the opposite end and the previous attackers backcheck.
coaching_points: Defenders look for a controlled first pass after winning possession.
Breakout targets stay ready and present their sticks.
Former attackers transition immediately into backcheckers.
Offense supports the puck with cutbacks and protection instead of forcing plays.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: Bentley Wall Cycling Drill
description: Two players work a pressured wall retrieval into a cycle. The first player retrieves and moves up the wall under coach pressure, cycles the puck down, then gets to the slot while the second player protects the puck and finds the return pass for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before each retrieval.
Use feet and body deception to protect the puck.
Cycle the puck firmly down the wall instead of softly bumping it.
First player gets off the wall and arrives in the slot as a shooting option.

title: Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game
description: A continuous 2-on-2 starts in one end. When the defending pair wins possession, it must connect the puck to the next pair waiting across the middle, who immediately attacks the opposite net while the previous offensive pair backchecks.
coaching_points: Transition immediately when possession changes.
Defenders pressure from inside-out with active sticks.
Use controlled direct or bank passes instead of throwing the puck away.
Offense moves and supports quickly to create a scoring chance before the defense sets.

title: Turn & Burn
description: Part 1 is a 3-on-2 rush started from a loose puck in the neutral zone. On the second whistle, the same three forwards track back to strip a coach near the blue line, get onside and immediately attack the same defenders again in another 3-on-2.
coaching_points: Forwards fill three lanes and work the puck toward middle ice.
Defenders manage gap and angle the rush outside.
Tracking forwards close with urgency before re-attacking.
Communicate through both the entry and the transition.

title: 3 on 2 Race to 5
description: Three forwards, two defenders and a goalie compete below the tops of the circles. Forwards score a point for a goal, defenders score by carrying the puck across the boundary, and the goalie scores by freezing the puck. New players enter after each point.
coaching_points: Race to establish possession first.
Forwards support underneath the puck and stay available.
Defense and goalie work together to kill the play.
Use the race-to-five scoring to keep intensity high.

title: Pass Through The Triangle Game
description: Three defenders form a triangle in the middle while three offensive players move around them. The offense earns success by timing passes through the triangle, then can finish the sequence with a shot on goal.
coaching_points: Keep moving to create new passing windows.
Communicate before the passing lane opens.
Players without the puck time their movement through the triangle.
Make the triangle smaller or activate defenders' sticks to raise difficulty.

title: 3 Player - Every Pass a One Touch
description: Three players recover a puck and keep it moving around the zone using only one-touch passes. If a player cannot complete a one-touch play, the next group enters. Coaches may also allow the group to finish on net.
coaching_points: Know the next passing option before the puck arrives.
Communicate constantly and keep sticks presented.
Stay in motion to keep lanes changing.
Add defenders or more players once the group can execute cleanly.

title: Ramsay 3 V 3 Race
description: Two separate 3-on-3 games run in opposite ends. On the whistle, all players race to a puck placed by the coach; the team that wins the puck attacks. A later whistle sends both groups to the opposite end to race for the next puck.
coaching_points: Compete hard to win the initial puck.
Offense supports the puck and creates outlets.
Defense keeps sticks in lanes.
Communicate through the race, possession and transition.

title: Oreo
description: A continuous 3-on-3. Offense tries to score while defense wins possession and passes to the next teammates waiting on the blue line. Once that pass connects, the new group attacks and the former offense becomes the defending team.
coaching_points: Offense supports the puck and stays available.
Defense uses active sticks and angles play outside.
Make the breakout pass under control.
Everyone communicates because roles change immediately.

title: Ride The Bull
description: Begin 2-on-2. A team must keep possession for eight straight seconds before earning a third teammate, creating a 3-on-2. The game then opens into a short attack before resetting.
coaching_points: Protect possession before forcing offense.
Use the teammate when pressure closes.
Move to support the puck carrier and create time.
Once the extra player joins, attack quickly before the defense adjusts.

title: 2 on 2 Gap Control
description: Two forwards attack two defenders from the neutral zone. The defenders close together and try to end the rush near the blue line while the forwards read whether to attack wide, protect the puck or move it through pressure to the second forward.
coaching_points: Defenders close in tandem and stay connected.
Lead with the stick to remove space and disrupt the puck carrier's hands.
Use efficient T-pushes and direct skating rather than unnecessary crossovers.
Forwards read the pressure and attack the available space.

title: 2 v 2 Activate the Point
description: Play 2-on-2 in the offensive zone with a point player available to the team in possession. After winning the puck, the attacking team must use the point before continuing the attack, allowing the point player to rotate or jump into space and create a temporary numbers advantage.
coaching_points: Use the point to change the picture for the defenders.
Point player activates with purpose rather than standing still.
Off-puck players keep moving to create new lanes.
On a turnover, transition through the point before attacking.

title: 3 v 3 Using the Weak Side to Shoot
description: A 3-on-3 possession game where the attack works to create a shot from the weak side. Off-puck players rotate into backside space while the puck carrier manipulates defenders and waits for a clean passing lane to the shooter.
coaching_points: Find backside shooting space instead of crowding the puck.
Keep moving if the lane is closed.
Use deception to hide behind defenders before popping into space.
Puck carrier and weak-side player read one another.

title: Escape the Corner Puck Protection
description: An offensive player retrieves a rimmed puck in the corner and protects it under controlled pressure for several seconds. On the whistle, the player must get the puck off the wall, escape the corner and attack the net while the defender tries to prevent the scoring chance.
coaching_points: Establish body position on the retrieval.
Keep feet moving while protecting the puck.
Use the defender's pressure and momentum to create separation.
Move the puck off the wall before exploding to the net.

title: Razor 1 on 1 Drill
description: One attacker and one defender compete inside a small area with four outside support passers. The attacker works through three separate pucks, using support, changes of speed and body position to protect possession and create shots.
coaching_points: Protect the puck away from the boards.
Change speed to create separation.
Use hips and body position to shield the puck.
Move to create support passing lanes.
Defender maintains good stick position and angle.

title: Goalie Rebound Game
description: Two goalies face angled nets with a shooter positioned between them. The shooter can fire at either goalie, and each goalie tries to control or steer rebounds toward the opposite net. The scoring format rewards rebound direction and concentration.
coaching_points: Track the puck before every release.
Stay square and balanced for unpredictable shots.
Direct rebounds intentionally instead of simply blocking them.
Compete while maintaining technical control.

title: 3 vs. 1 Keep Away Game
description: Three attackers keep possession against one defender in a defined area. The offense wins by maintaining possession until the whistle; the defender scores by stripping the puck and exiting the area or forcing the puck out.
coaching_points: Play with the head up and sticks available.
Move to open space instead of standing still.
Use deception to move the defender.
Defender stays controlled with the stick in passing lanes rather than chasing.

title: Gates of Buffalo 3 on 3 Game
description: Teams score by completing passes through small gates placed around the playing area. Players may not use the same gate twice in a row, which forces movement, scanning, communication and new passing angles.
coaching_points: Move constantly to open space.
Find new passing lanes rather than forcing the same gate.
Communicate verbally and with body language.
Shrink the gates or area to increase decision speed.

title: Finnish 5 Puck Progression
description: A progression for three to five players in a confined area. It starts with skating and puck-control variations, then adds one to five active pucks, and finishes with keep-away situations such as 4-on-1 and 3-on-2.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and move to open space.
Communicate before passes arrive.
Add pucks gradually as awareness improves.
Use obstacles or smaller space to increase difficulty.
Value decisions and scanning over memorizing routes.

title: D-Zone Gates
description: A multi-net defensive-zone game where offensive players use space behind the nets to move defenders and create chances in front. The defending group works on behind-the-net coverage, communication, middle protection and far-post responsibility.
coaching_points: Decide clearly whether to flush or hand off behind the net.
Protect the middle first.
Use stick and body position to deny passes through the house.
Offense uses behind-the-net possession to move the coverage.

title: 2 v 1 Small Space to Big Space
description: Two attackers play against one defender. One attacker begins in the crowded puck area while the second attacker stays in open ice. The offense works to move the puck out of pressure and into the bigger space before attacking the net.
coaching_points: Recognize where the open ice is.
Support the puck from outside the pressure.
Use chips, wraps or direct passes as needed.
Defender keeps the stick in the passing lane and protects the middle.

title: 3 v 2 Small Space to Big Space
description: Three attackers play against two defenders, with two attackers initially working in the crowded puck area and the third attacker positioned in open space. The offense must recognize the pressure and move the puck into the larger space before finishing.
coaching_points: Use the third attacker as the escape valve.
Support the puck instead of standing in coverage.
Move the puck before pressure closes.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and communicate.

title: Angle Shooter
description: A player attacks across the ice and shoots, then immediately stops and becomes the defender against the next puck carrier coming from the opposite side. The defender works back through the middle and angles the attacker to the outside.
coaching_points: Transition from offense to defense immediately after the shot.
Work through the middle before applying the angle.
Keep feet moving and stick on the puck.
Force the attacker toward a low-percentage outside lane.

title: Red Line Angle
description: Two players race without the puck toward the red line. The coach then sends a puck into the zone, creating a 1-on-1 where the puck-side player attacks and the other player must gain inside position and angle the rush outside.
coaching_points: Race hard to establish position.
Defender works for inside body position.
Keep feet moving through the angle.
Maintain stick-on-puck pressure and steer the attacker wide.

title: Takeaway Transition Train
description: A continuous takeaway drill along the wall. One player carries the puck while a trailing defender angles from behind, attacks the backside of the puck, wins it and immediately accelerates off the wall into open ice. The same skill can also be run from a corner.
coaching_points: Attack the backside of the puck instead of reaching through the body.
Keep the stick on the ice while angling to remove passing lanes.
After the takeaway, get off the wall immediately.
Explode into transition without gliding.

title: Flynn 2 on 1 x 3
description: Three consecutive 2-on-1 situations in one repetition: a low 2-on-1 near the net, a regroup into a long 2-on-1 rush, then a final net-front 2-on-1 created from a puck played down from the blue line.
coaching_points: Attack tight-space 2-on-1s with quick hands and decisions.
Forwards track back inside before the long rush.
Defense manages gap and angles to predictable ice.
At the net front, one forward screens while the second stays available for a pass or rebound.

title: Big Boy Battle
description: A competitive low-zone battle progression that begins 1-on-1 and advances to 2-on-2. Offense scores by creating cutbacks and goals while defenders earn success through pins, clean wins and controlled exits above the pylons.
coaching_points: Win the puck race with balance and inside leverage.
Use strong wall-battle posture and pins.
Defenders exit under control instead of simply chipping the puck away.
Offense uses cutbacks, protection and direct net attacks.
Transition immediately when possession changes.

title: 2 on 1 Strip Drill
description: Two forwards attack a defender on entry. The defender works to surf, own the middle and force the puck outside. After the first rush, the forwards reload and a second puck creates another 2-on-1 so the defender must gap up again.
coaching_points: Defender dictates the rush by skating forward when possible.
Surf from the inside and protect the middle.
Tracking forwards reload hard from behind.
Keep the stick on the ice to close lanes and create takeaways.

title: BC 3 on 2 Breakouts
description: A continuous breakout sequence where two forecheckers apply pressure to two defensemen plus a low supporting forward. The breakout group must escape without rimming the puck, exit with possession and activate the next repetition through the neutral zone.
coaching_points: Beat pressure with feet, support and clean puck movement.
Low forward stays available underneath the puck.
Forecheckers apply real pressure to force decisions.
Use deception and puck protection instead of automatic rims.
Communicate through the breakout.

title: Drummond Regroup
description: A continuous no-shot warm-up centered on regroups under pressure. A forward pressures a defenseman while another forward supports underneath, creating a support triangle. The puck then moves across to the next defenseman and the pattern repeats.
coaching_points: Maintain proper spacing and timing in the support triangle.
Defense invites pressure before moving the puck.
Support forward stays low and underneath.
Keep feet moving through pressure.
Use quick-ups, flat passes or skating when the read is available.

title: Thomas Holmstrom SAG
description: A competitive net-front game where three attackers battle two or three defenders inside a marked box while a shooter releases pucks from high in the zone. The focus is screens, tips, rebounds, box-outs and traffic management.
coaching_points: Offense wins inside position quickly and creates layers of traffic.
Defenders maintain inside leverage and execute strong box-outs.
Shooter keeps pucks purposeful and low when looking for tips.
Goalie tracks through traffic and battles for sightlines.

title: 1 v 1 Angling Cone Touch Game
description: Two players react to a puck placed to one side, skate around their cones and compete 1-on-1. The puck carrier tries to touch the opponent's cone with the puck while the defender angles toward the boards and works to win possession.
coaching_points: Take a controlled angle to the puck or puck carrier.
Time the route instead of over-skating.
Use body position to shield or steal the puck.
Defender forces play outside.

title: Own the Dot
description: The puck is placed behind the offensive player. The attacker must protect the puck without immediately touching it while the defender works to steal possession using deception, stick lifts and leverage.
coaching_points: Offense stays between the defender and the puck.
Look at the opponent instead of staring at the puck.
Use body position to shield.
Defender uses skating deception, stick lifts and leverage to win position.

title: Power Play from 5 v 1 to 5 v 4
description: Begin 5-on-1 in the offensive zone. At timed or random intervals, the coach adds penalty killers until the game progresses through 5-on-2, 5-on-3 and finally 5-on-4.
coaching_points: Power play moves the puck quickly and looks for shots off the pass.
Net-front player screens and works for tips or redirects.
Penalty killers protect the middle and keep sticks in lanes.
Add defenders at different intervals to change the read.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: 3 v 3 Keep Possession
description: A 3-on-3 possession game where each completed pass can score a point. The possession team moves and supports the puck while the defending team creates a turnover and immediately tries to establish its own possession.
coaching_points: Skate to win space and become a passing option.
Provide close support in pressure.
Keep the puck moving rather than holding it.
React immediately after turnovers to regain or secure possession.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: Rabbit and Coyote
description: Two players pass back and forth outside a circle. On the whistle they enter the circle; the player with the puck protects possession while the other player tries to steal it. Possession can change multiple times before the rep ends.
coaching_points: Present a clean passing target before the battle begins.
Use body, stick and feet to protect the puck.
Use tight turns and cutbacks to escape pressure.
Defender keeps the stick down and attacks the puck.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: 1 v 1 Defend The House
description: A confined 1-on-1 below the top of the circle. The attacker tries to score while the defender creates a turnover and exits through a gate. A new puck can be introduced immediately after a defensive win.
coaching_points: Defender keeps a tight gap and stays between puck and net.
Keep the stick on the ice and angle play outside.
Use blade-on-blade pressure to create turnovers.
Attacker protects the puck away from the defender and uses deception to attack the middle.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: Oiler Protect Drill
description: A two-part 1-on-1 progression. First, the defender uses inside-out footwork to angle an attacker wide on a rush. A second puck is then placed into the corner for an immediate live battle and net attack.
coaching_points: Defender stays inside-out and uses stick and body angle to steer the rush.
Force the attacker wide before closing.
On the corner rep, deny the back of the net and defend through the inside hip.
Attacker gets off the wall quickly and protects the puck under pressure.

title: Early Box Outs
description: Two forwards and two defensemen work a defensive-zone sequence that finishes with a point shot. The weak-side defenseman establishes body position early on the net-front forward before the shot is released.
coaching_points: Know where the puck is while maintaining body position.
Start the box-out early, not at the top of the crease.
Drive the forward toward the near post and away from middle ice.
If beaten to the front, transition to fronting the puck and remove the screen.

title: Olympic 1 on 1
description: The forward attacks straight down the ice while the defenseman backpedals to the red line, pivots, matches speed and closes the gap before defending the rush live to the net.
coaching_points: Defense gets back to the red line quickly before pivoting.
Accelerate into the first forward stride after the pivot.
Maintain a tight gap and confidence in the feet.
Efficient skating creates better gap control.

title: Swoop 2 v 2
description: Two forwards swoop around the center group before attacking two defensemen. The defenders cannot react until identifying the puck carrier, then communicate through crosses while protecting the middle on the live 2-on-2 rush.
coaching_points: Defense communicates early and stays connected.
Protect the middle and keep attackers outside.
Let forwards cross while defenders maintain lanes when possible.
Maintain useful gap through the transition.
A second puck can create a net-front box-out progression.

title: Double Double Islander
description: A defensive-zone support drill where a defenseman contains the puck carrier in the corner while a supporting forward reads whether to hold the slot lane or double the puck to create a turnover.
coaching_points: Defenseman contains first before asking for support.
Supporting forward doubles only when the passing lane is safe to leave.
Protect the slot until the moment to attack.
End the play quickly once two defenders have established leverage.

title: Patty Roy 1 on 1
description: A corner 1-on-1 where the forward retrieves a spotted puck and attacks the net while the defender contains, maintains inside position and steers the attacker away from dangerous ice before closing the gap.
coaching_points: Contain first and prevent access behind the net.
Push the attacker toward outside ice.
Lead with the stick and keep it on the puck.
Close physically only when the moment is right, then return to an active stick.

title: 1 v 1 Gap Control and Angling Drill
description: The coach spots a puck for a forward while the defenseman first touches the blue line, then closes space while skating forward as long as possible. The defender uses angle, stick position and body control to dictate the live 1-on-1.
coaching_points: Defend forward as long as the play allows.
Close space early and maintain a tight gap.
Keep an active stick to reduce options.
Do not open the hips unless the attacker earns the turn.
Recover only when necessary.

title: Soft Catch Behind the Net to Attack
description: One player rims a puck behind the net while the opposite player receives it with a soft catch across the body, curls with momentum and finds the original passer arriving in the slot for a quick shot.
coaching_points: Receive with the body slightly off the wall so both escape directions remain available.
Let the puck travel across the body before catching it.
Maintain skating momentum through the catch.
Slot player times the route and presents the stick early.
Work both forehand and backhand sides.

title: Major Soft Catch to Shot
description: Players pass to a coach, receive a soft catch around an obstacle, move the puck to the opposite-side player, circle and receive another soft catch before finishing with a quick shot.
coaching_points: Catch the puck in stride with it crossing the body before contact.
Keep the stick presented as a target.
Maintain speed through both catches.
Work both sides so players handle forehand and backhand receptions.

title: Double Soft Catch to Shot
description: A half-ice skill drill where a player exchanges two passes with a coach while moving around an obstacle, receiving both with a soft catch across the body before finishing with a quick shot.
coaching_points: Catch each pass in stride instead of stopping the puck.
Use the across-body catch to load the next movement.
Communicate and present the stick.
Run both sides to work forehand and backhand receptions.
Stagger reps so the goalie is set.

title: Stick-Led Pivot
description: Players skate backward along a painted line and use the stick pull to lead the hips through a backward-to-forward pivot, then accelerate to the next line. The painted lines help expose drifting and inefficient mechanics.
coaching_points: Stick pull and skate opening happen together.
Drive the top hand across the body to help rotate the hips.
Stay on the painted line through the pivot.
Eliminate any pause or hitch before the first forward stride.
Progress from controlled reps to high speed.

title: The Riga
description: A goalie tracking drill where the puck moves laterally to force angle changes and visual attachment. After the first shot, the goalie touches the near post, recovers position and prepares for a second shot.
coaching_points: Maintain visual attachment throughout lateral movement.
Use efficient edgework to stay square rather than drifting.
Arrive set before the shot.
Recover to the post and re-establish angle quickly for the second shot.
